root_cause.text: The `vrealloc_node_align()` function unconditionally copies `old_size` bytes into a newly allocated buffer of `size` bytes without checking if `size < old_size`, causing a buffer overflow when shrinking allocations on the reallocation path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `memcpy(n, p, old_size)` to `memcpy(n, p, min(size, old_size))` in the `vrealloc_node_align_noprof()` function. The CVE description explicitly states: "the code allocates a new object of 'size' bytes and then memcpy()s 'old_size' bytes into it. If the request is to shrink the object (size < old_size), this results in an out-of-bounds write on the new buffer." This occurs specifically on the `need_realloc` path when NUMA node or alignment constraints force a new allocation even during shrinking operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential buffer overflow in vrealloc by limiting memcpy to the minimum of old and new allocation sizes.
intent_record.what: Changed the third argument of memcpy from 'old_size' to 'min(size, old_size)' in the vrealloc_node_align_noprof function.
intent_record.how: This prevents buffer overflow when copying data from the old allocation to the new allocation. If the new size is smaller than the old size, memcpy will now only copy up to the new size, preventing writes beyond the bounds of the newly allocated memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `vrealloc_noprof()` contains proper size checking before copying. At lines 52-57, there is an explicit check `if (size <= old_size)` that handles the shrinking case by returning the original pointer after zeroing spare memory if needed. The vulnerable copy operation at line 66 (`memcpy(n, p, old_size)`) only executes when `size > old_size` (in the growth path), which is safe because `old_size` bytes are being copied into a buffer of `size` bytes where `size > old_size`. The root cause vulnerability (copying `old_size` bytes into a smaller `size` buffer) is prevented by the conditional logic that returns early when `size <= old_size`.
